architectural_implications.after: Prompts become thin, model-generation-scoped artifacts, with harness code and tool descriptions carrying capability and a deliberate pruning step at each model upgrade.
architectural_implications.before: Prompt templates are treated as durable, additive assets; each new failure adds another example or negative constraint.
architectural_implications.consequence: New maintenance workflow: on model upgrade, actively delete prompt content and re-measure, rather than preserving prompts for backward compatibility.
architectural_implications.observation: System prompts encode constraints that smarter models can infer themselves, so the prompt layer accumulates redundant scaffolding across generations.

architectural_implications.after: Context representation, action interface, and memory/compaction treated as pluggable dimensions chosen against task requirements.
architectural_implications.before: Harness built monolithically around one default modality (e.g., screenshot-only, human-like clicking).
architectural_implications.consequence: Enables per-task harness selection and A/B benchmarking across the matrix rather than a single global harness design.
architectural_implications.observation: Browser agent harnesses have at least three independent design axes (context storage, action archetype, auxiliary features).

architectural_implications.after: Context lifecycle (what is stored, what is compacted, what subagents hold) becomes an explicit, named subsystem.
architectural_implications.before: Context handling treated as an implicit byproduct of the transcript format.
architectural_implications.consequence: Compaction policy becomes a first-class reliability concern: incorrect compaction silently removes the memory an agent needs mid-task.
architectural_implications.observation: Compaction and subagents are harness-level features governing context lifecycle, and context storage strategy is an open question for browser agents.

article_ideas.angle: Reframe prompt bloat as versioned technical debt with an explicit prune-and-re-measure step at every model upgrade, using the ~80% Claude Code prompt reduction as the worked example of what deletion actually looks like.
article_ideas.audience: Agent and platform engineers maintaining long-lived system prompts across model upgrades
article_ideas.based_on: System prompt design inverts as models improve
article_ideas.thesis: Enumerated constraints in a system prompt are rent paid on one specific model generation's weaknesses; when the model improves, those constraints stop being insurance and start being interference, so the correct engineering act at every upgrade is deletion backed by re-measurement, not preservation for backward compatibility.
article_ideas.title: Your System Prompt Is a Model-Generation Artifact, Not an Asset

article_ideas.angle: Show how a single interface choice (chat vs code execution with fetch and grep) flips a task from failure to trivial, and argue that benchmark reports without a harness specification are unfalsifiable.
article_ideas.audience: Eval designers, model-selection decision makers, agent platform teams
article_ideas.based_on: Capability overhang: models possess latent capabilities that only surface when given an execution environment
article_ideas.thesis: Capability measured in a chat interface is not predictive of capability in an execution harness, so any evaluation that fixes the interface is measuring the interface and reporting it as the model; the unit of evaluation must be the model-plus-harness pair.
article_ideas.title: Benchmark the Harness, Not the Model

article_ideas.angle: Translate the known/unknown matrix into concrete prompt artifacts (blindspot pass, implementation notes, deviation logging) and argue they target a failure class that generic clarification advice does not touch.
article_ideas.audience: Agent developers and tech leads deploying coding agents onto unfamiliar repositories
article_ideas.based_on: The unknown matrix (known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, unknown-unknowns)
article_ideas.thesis: When an agent executes an abstract prompt against a real codebase, the dominant failure is not instruction-following but unstated requirements, and the fix is a mandated pass whose only job is to enumerate what the requester failed to say — a different intervention than 'ask clarifying questions'.
article_ideas.title: The Map Is Not the Territory: Ship Elicitation Passes, Not Better Instructions

article_ideas.angle: Decompose the harness into its axes, show why context representation is only meaningful relative to the chosen action space, and turn the unresolved context-storage question into an explicit benchmark plan.
article_ideas.audience: Browser agent and computer-use harness engineers
article_ideas.thesis: Context storage, action-execution archetype, and auxiliary memory features are separable design axes, but most browser agent harnesses hard-code one modality stack by default; treating the axes independently lets teams choose per-task harnesses and benchmark the cross product instead of defending a single global design.
article_ideas.title: Browser Agent Harnesses Are Three Decisions, and You Are Making Them All Implicitly

connections.relationship: execution tooling is the unlock mechanism that converts latent capability into observable task performance
shrinking prompts is the migration action implied by rising native judgment
elicitation prompts are the mitigation for abstraction/reality mismatch

evidence_quotes.text: Chat models failing to name Pokémon ending in 'aw' until given a coding environment to fetch and grep the data.
Models know things empirically that chat interfaces fail to extract.
Capabilities grow spikily rather than smoothly.

core_insights.generalization: Any intelligence evaluation should be run inside the target harness, since capability measured in one interface is not predictive of capability in another.
core_insights.insight: Capability overhang: models possess latent capabilities that only surface when given an execution environment (e.g., code execution + grep) rather than a chat interface; capability growth is spiky, not smooth. The Pokémon-'aw' case shows a chat model failing a retrieval-style task that becomes trivial once the model can write a script to fetch and grep data.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It reframes agent capability as a property of the model-plus-harness pair, not the model alone. Engineers who benchmark a model only in chat will systematically underestimate it and may over-engineer prompts or tool scaffolding to compensate for limitations that execution tools would dissolve.

evidence_quotes.text: Claude 5 models require smaller system prompts and fewer examples because of better model judgment.
Removing 80% of system prompts from Claude Code as models got smarter.
Constraints are being replaced by judgment and tool capability.

core_insights.generalization: Prompt/constraint scaffolding should be treated as versioned technical debt tied to a specific model generation, reviewed and deleted at each upgrade rather than accumulated.
core_insights.insight: System prompt design inverts as models improve: newer Claude models need substantially smaller system prompts and fewer few-shot examples because native judgment replaces enumerated constraints. Anthropic reportedly removed about 80% of Claude Code's system prompt over model generations.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Prompt bloat is not neutral — it is a maintenance liability and can degrade behavior on stronger models. This gives a concrete heuristic (cut prompts hard when upgrading model generations) and a migration task for every agent codebase.

evidence_quotes.text: Categorizing knowledge into known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, and unknown-unknowns helps refine agent prompts.
Prompting requires helping models find their unknown unknowns.
Prompts like blindspot passes and implementation notes unearth hidden edge cases.

core_insights.generalization: Agents operating on underspecified real-world artifacts should be given explicit elicitation passes whose only job is to enumerate what the requester failed to state.
core_insights.insight: The unknown matrix (known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, unknown-unknowns) is used as a prompt-engineering instrument: prompts like 'blindspot pass' exist specifically to surface unknown-unknowns, and agents are asked to log implementation notes and deviations when the abstract prompt (map) collides with the real codebase (territory).
core_insights.why_it_matters: It converts an abstract epistemics framing into named, reusable prompt patterns that target a specific failure class — agent confidently executing a spec it never actually understood — which is different from generic 'ask clarifying questions' advice.

evidence_quotes.text: Context storage (screenshots, DOM, diffs, annotations)
Action execution (human-like, computer-like, coding agent, bash agent)
Harness features (subagents, compaction, memory)

core_insights.generalization: For any perception-action agent, separate the observation encoding decision from the action interface decision and evaluate the cross product rather than a single stacked default.
core_insights.insight: Browser agent harness design decomposes into three separable architectural axes: context storage (all screenshots vs DOM diffing vs bounding-box annotations), action execution archetype (human-like, computer-like, coding agent, bash agent), and auxiliary harness features (subagents, compaction, memory).
core_insights.why_it_matters: Treating context representation and action-space shape as independent decisions gives engineers an explicit design space instead of committing implicitly to one modality (e.g., always screenshots). The choice of action archetype strongly constrains what context representation is even useful.

evidence_quotes.text: Transitioning from Opus 4 (calling AskUserQuestion with difficulty) to Opus 4.5 (interviewing users) to Opus 4.8 (building HTML reports and quizzes).
Use HTML artifacts instead of raw markdown for complex multi-step agent plans.

core_insights.generalization: Agent interaction surfaces should be re-validated per model generation; the artifact format an agent produces is part of its interface contract and its usability for verification by humans.
core_insights.insight: Emergent tool use appears to evolve rapidly across model generations, changing the interaction contract itself: from asking the user questions (crucially, with difficulty) to interviewing users, to producing HTML reports and quizzes as structured artifacts; likewise HTML artifacts are recommended over raw markdown for complex multi-step agent plans.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If the model's natural interaction modality shifts per generation, harness features built around the old modality (e.g., markdown plan rendering, one-shot clarifying questions) become stale, and output-format choices like HTML become an agent-design decision rather than a presentation detail.

evidence_quotes.text: AI models are grown, not designed.
Treat LLM development more like biology than physics; rules are empirical and non-deterministic.

core_insights.generalization: For artifacts produced by optimization rather than specification, treat behavior as an observed natural phenomenon: build probing and regression harnesses before writing prescriptive rules.
core_insights.insight: Agent development should be treated as biology rather than physics: models are grown, not designed, so capabilities and rules must be discovered empirically through training and testing rather than derived from deterministic specification.
core_insights.why_it_matters: This justifies an empirical, measurement-driven engineering loop (probe, observe, then codify) over spec-first prompt authoring, and predicts that harness rules will be non-transferable between model versions and must be re-derived.

evidence_quotes.text: Chat models failing to name Pokémon ending in 'aw' until given a coding environment to fetch and grep the data.
Models know things empirically that chat interfaces fail to extract.
Equipping models with execution tools bridges capability gaps.

deep_dives.trigger_insight: Capability overhang: models possess latent capabilities that only surface when given an execution environment
deep_dives.why: The canonical Pokemon-'aw' example confounds execution, retrieval, and scripting in a single anecdote. If the unlock is really 'grep-able retrieval' rather than 'a bash tool', then harness builders should invest in retrieval surfaces instead of a general-purpose shell, and blast-radius concerns over broad action spaces change shape.

evidence_quotes.text: Claude 5 models require smaller system prompts and fewer examples because of better model judgment.
Removing 80% of system prompts from Claude Code as models got smarter.
Constraints are being replaced by judgment and tool capability.

deep_dives.topic: Prompt shrinkage as a per-generation migration obligation
deep_dives.trigger_insight: System prompt design inverts as models improve
deep_dives.why: If the boundary is real and moves every generation, then every agent codebase carries prompt debt that must be audited and deleted at each upgrade rather than preserved for backward compatibility. This converts prompt authoring from an additive art into a versioned pruning workflow with measurable acceptance criteria.

What is the optimal context storage strategy for browser agents?

deep_dives.topic: Context representation for browser agents as an open architectural variable
deep_dives.trigger_insight: What is the optimal context storage strategy for browser agents?
deep_dives.why: The summary names the candidate representations but states no comparative result, while also noting that raw context volume drives compaction pressure. Committing implicitly to screenshots (or DOM) locks in both a token bill and a memory-loss risk profile that may be avoidable.

evidence_quotes.text: Harness features (subagents, compaction, memory)
incorrect compaction silently removes the memory an agent needs mid-task

deep_dives.why: Compaction is treated in the summary as a harness feature and a risk but never as a testable policy. Because compaction failure is silent — the agent simply behaves as if it never knew something — it requires a regression harness rather than prompt-level intuition.

evidence_quotes.text: Prompting requires helping models find their unknown unknowns.
Models frequently run into unknowns when given abstract instructions.
Prompts like blindspot passes and implementation notes unearth hidden edge cases.

project_ideas.based_on: Capability overhang: models possess latent capabilities that only surface when given an execution environment
project_ideas.hypothesis: The capability gain attributed to 'giving the model a bash tool' is mainly attributable to retrieval-and-grep access, not to code execution itself; a retrieval-only tool will recover most of the gain on parametric-recall tasks while a bare code-execution tool without data access will not.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate per arm, with the retrieval-only arm compared against the full-execution arm; a large gap in favor of full execution falsifies the retrieval-only hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Overhang Isolator
project_ideas.poc: Build a controlled task battery in three arms — (a) chat-only parametric recall, (b) chat + retrieval/grep access with no arbitrary execution, (c) chat + full script execution and fetch/grep — over datasets where the model demonstrably 'knows' the answer but cannot surface it in chat.

project_ideas.based_on: Claude 5 models require smaller system prompts and fewer examples because of better model judgment.
project_ideas.hypothesis: For a fixed agent task suite, a system prompt pruned by roughly 80% with minimal few-shot examples matches or beats the pre-prune prompt on a newer model generation, and any regressions are concentrated in a small, identifiable set of instruction-following cases rather than spread evenly.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success delta between prompt tiers per model generation, plus the count and identity of regressed instruction-following cases; a systematic pruned-tier loss falsifies the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Prompt Debt Auditor
project_ideas.poc: Version-control two prompt tiers (full and pruned) for one agent, run both against an identical task suite on successive model generations, and produce a per-case diff report tagging each prompt clause as retained, deleted, or inverted.

project_ideas.based_on: What is the optimal context storage strategy for browser agents?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Context representation and action-execution archetype interact strongly enough that no single representation dominates; the best-performing (context, action) pair changes across task families, so a per-task harness selection beats any global default.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success, tokens, and latency per matrix cell, plus whether the argmax cell differs across task families; a single cell dominating all families on all axes falsifies the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Harness Cross-Product Bench
project_ideas.poc: Implement a browser agent harness with pluggable context backends (full screenshots, DOM diffs, bounding-box annotations) and pluggable action interfaces, then run the cross product on one shared task suite with token and latency accounting per cell.

project_ideas.based_on: How can compaction be automated without losing critical agent memory?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Aggressive compaction causes silent, measurable memory loss on long-horizon tasks, and retention rules keyed to task-critical facts, logged deviations, and prior decisions recover most of the lost success at a fraction of the uncompacted token cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Success rate and post-compaction recall of planted facts as a function of compaction aggressiveness; retention rules that do not beat naive compaction falsify the hypothesis.
project_ideas.name: Compaction Memory-Loss Regression
project_ideas.poc: Construct long-horizon tasks with planted critical facts and mandated deviation logging, then run them under a sweep of compaction aggressiveness settings with and without the retention criteria enabled.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Thariq Shihipar
  • Channel: Browserbase
  • Main topic: Building and prompting AI agents (specifically Claude)
  • Purpose: To explain the methodologies, empirical discoveries, and challenges in harness engineering and prompting to unhobble Claude in agentic workflows. Thariq Shihipar from Anthropic discusses the process of building AI agents, introducing concepts like capability overhang, spiky capability growth, system prompt design evolution, and unknown matrices in prompting.

Topic Map

Introduction to Unhobbling Claude

  • Explanation: Introduction of the speaker and the main theme of building agents, harness engineering, and unhobbling Claude.
  • Key claims:
    • AI models are grown, not designed.
    • Agent capabilities depend heavily on the harness and prompting.
  • Examples:
    • Claude Code and bash tool integration.
  • Terminology:
    • harness engineering
    • capability overhang
    • unhobbling Claude
  • Why it matters: Sets the stage for understanding that model intelligence is unlocked through proper scaffolding.

Capability Overhang and Spiky Capabilities

  • Explanation: Models possess hidden capabilities that only emerge when given the right tools and execution environments.
  • Key claims:
    • Models know things empirically that chat interfaces fail to extract.
    • Capabilities grow spikily rather than smoothly.
  • Examples:
    • Chat models failing to name Pokémon ending in 'aw' until given a coding environment to fetch and grep the data.
  • Terminology:
    • capability overhang
    • spiky capability
  • Why it matters: Explains why giving models execution tools unlocks dormant intelligence.

System Prompt Design Evolution

  • Explanation: How system prompts evolved from large prompts with many examples to smaller prompts relying on model judgment.
  • Key claims:
    • Claude 5 models require smaller system prompts and fewer examples because of better model judgment.
    • Constraints are being replaced by judgment and tool capability.
  • Examples:
    • Removing 80% of system prompts from Claude Code as models got smarter.
  • Terminology:
    • system prompt design
    • compaction
    • judgment vs constraints
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates how prompting strategy changes as underlying models advance.

The Map is not the Territory

  • Explanation: The challenge of navigating unknown coding environments and codebases where prompts are abstract maps and the codebase is the territory.
  • Key claims:
    • Models frequently run into unknowns when given abstract instructions.
    • Prompting requires helping models find their unknown unknowns.
  • Examples:
    • Blindspot pass prompts, implementation notes, and quizzes.
  • Terminology:
    • unknown matrix
    • blindspot pass
    • implementation notes
  • Why it matters: Provides practical prompt patterns for agentic development tasks.

Browser Agents and Harness Engineering Choices

  • Explanation: Designing harnesses for browser agents, including context storage and action execution choices.
  • Key claims:
    • Building browser agents involves major architectural choices around context storage and action execution.
    • Different agent archetypes range from acting like humans to acting like coding or bash agents.
  • Examples:
    • Storing all screenshots vs DOM diffing vs bounding box annotations.
  • Terminology:
    • browser agents
    • context management
    • subagents
    • compaction
  • Why it matters: Offers a structural framework for building custom browser and web agents.

Key Points

Models are grown, not designed

  • Explanation: AI models are trained with data and feedback rather than engineered with deterministic rules.
  • Evidence: Performance on specific tasks is discovered empirically through training and testing.
  • Practical implication: Developers must discover model capabilities empirically rather than assuming limitations from pure chat benchmarks.

Evolution of System Prompts

  • Explanation: As models get smarter, system prompts should shrink, replacing strict negative constraints with guidance on judgment.
  • Evidence: Claude 5 models perform better with smaller system prompts and fewer few-shot examples.
  • Practical implication: Do not overload modern models with exhaustive examples; leverage their native understanding and tool descriptions.

The Unknown Matrix

  • Explanation: Categorizing knowledge into known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, and unknown-unknowns helps refine agent prompts.
  • Evidence: Prompts like blindspot passes and implementation notes unearth hidden edge cases.
  • Practical implication: Design agent harnesses that allow models to ask clarifying questions or log deviations.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

The Unknown Matrix

  • How it works: A 2x2 matrix categorizing user and model awareness into knowns and unknowns to improve prompt engineering.
  • Components:
    • Known-Knowns (What do I want?)
    • Known-Unknowns (What haven't I figured out yet?)
    • Unknown-Knowns (What's so obvious I'd never write it down?)
    • Unknown-Unknowns (What haven't I considered at all?)
  • When to use: When prompting coding or browser agents on complex tasks where requirements are ambiguous.

Browser Agent Architecture Choices

  • How it works: A decision framework for structuring browser agent harnesses across context storage, action execution, and auxiliary features.
  • Components:
    • Context storage (screenshots, DOM, diffs, annotations)
    • Action execution (human-like, computer-like, coding agent, bash agent)
    • Harness features (subagents, compaction, memory)
  • When to use: When designing and engineering web navigation agents.

Examples & Case Studies

Chat models failed to list Pokémon whose names ended in 'aw', but Claude Code wrote a python script to fetch all Pokémon and grep the result.

  • Illustrates: Capability overhang and the power of giving models code execution arms.
  • Lesson: Equipping models with execution tools bridges capability gaps.

Transitioning from Opus 4 (calling AskUserQuestion with difficulty) to Opus 4.5 (interviewing users) to Opus 4.8 (building HTML reports and quizzes).

  • Illustrates: The emergence of agentic properties and structured artifact generation.
  • Lesson: Emergent tool use evolves rapidly across model generations.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Use blindspot pass prompts to help models uncover unknown unknowns in codebases.
    • Require agents to maintain implementation notes and log deviations.
    • Use HTML artifacts instead of raw markdown for complex multi-step agent plans.
  • Strategic:
    • Treat LLM development more like biology than physics; rules are empirical and non-deterministic.
    • Reduce system prompt bloat as newer, smarter models are integrated.
    • Bridge the gap between the abstract map (prompt) and the actual territory (codebase/browser).
  • Questions to investigate:
    • What is the optimal context storage strategy for browser agents?
    • How can compaction be automated without losing critical agent memory?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Models are grown, not designed. (conceptual)
  • 80% of system prompts were removed from Claude Code while maintaining or improving performance. (anecdotal)

Notable Quotes

"Models are grown, not designed." "What contains them is us — the harness we put in, and the way we prompt them." "It's closer to a biology, than a physics."

Compressed Summary

  • AI models exhibit capability overhang where tools unlock dormant capabilities.
  • System prompt design shifts from rigid constraints to model judgment as models improve.
  • Managing unknown unknowns requires structured prompts like blindspot passes and implementation notes.
  • Browser agent design requires careful architectural choices around context storage and action execution.
  • Keywords: agents, prompting, harness, claude, browserbase
  • Core insight: Building effective AI agents requires shifting from rigid rule-based constraints to empowering models with execution tools, smaller system prompts, and structured context management.

- **Explanation**: How system prompts evolved from large prompts with many examples to smaller prompts relying on model judgment.
- **Key claims**:
  - Claude 5 models require smaller system prompts and fewer examples because of better model judgment.
  - Constraints are being replaced by judgment and tool capability.
- **Examples**:
  - Removing 80% of system prompts from Claude Code as models got smarter.
- **Terminology**:
  - system prompt design
  - compaction
  - judgment vs constraints
- **Why it matters**: Demonstrates how prompting strategy changes as underlying models advance.
### The Map is not the Territory
- **Explanation**: The challenge of navigating unknown coding environments and codebases where prompts are abstract maps and the codebase is the territory.
- **Key claims**:
  - Models frequently run into unknowns when given abstract instructions.
  - Prompting requires helping models find their unknown unknowns.
- **Examples**:
  - Blindspot pass prompts, implementation notes, and quizzes.
- **Terminology**:
  - unknown matrix
  - blindspot pass
  - implementation notes
- **Why it matters**: Provides practical prompt patterns for agentic development tasks.
### Browser Agents and Harness Engineering Choices
- **Explanation**: Designing harnesses for browser agents, including context storage and action execution choices.
- **Key claims**:
  - Building browser agents involves major architectural choices around context storage and action execution.
  - Different agent archetypes range from acting like humans to acting like coding or bash agents.
- **Examples**:
  - Storing all screenshots vs DOM diffing vs bounding box annotations.
- **Terminology**:
  - browser agents
  - context management
  - subagents
  - compaction
- **Why it matters**: Offers a structural framework for building custom browser and web agents.
## Key Points
### Models are grown, not designed
- **Explanation**: AI models are trained with data and feedback rather than engineered with deterministic rules.
- **Evidence**: Performance on specific tasks is discovered empirically through training and testing.
- **Practical implication**: Developers must discover model capabilities empirically rather than assuming limitations from pure chat benchmarks.
### Evolution of System Prompts
- **Explanation**: As models get smarter, system prompts should shrink, replacing strict negative constraints with guidance on judgment.
- **Evidence**: Claude 5 models perform better with smaller system prompts and fewer few-shot examples.
- **Practical implication**: Do not overload modern models with exhaustive examples; leverage their native understanding and tool descriptions.
### The Unknown Matrix
- **Explanation**: Categorizing knowledge into known-knowns, known-unknowns, unknown-knowns, and unknown-unknowns helps refine agent prompts.
- **Evidence**: Prompts like blindspot passes and implementation notes unearth hidden edge cases.
- **Practical implication**: Design agent harnesses that allow models to ask clarifying questions or log deviations.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### The Unknown Matrix
- **How it works**: A 2x2 matrix categorizing user and model awareness into knowns and unknowns to improve prompt engineering.
- **Components**:
  - Known-Knowns (What do I want?)
  - Known-Unknowns (What haven't I figured out yet?)
  - Unknown-Knowns (What's so obvious I'd never write it down?)
  - Unknown-Unknowns (What haven't I considered at all?)
- **When to use**: When prompting coding or browser agents on complex tasks where requirements are ambiguous.
### Browser Agent Architecture Choices
- **How it works**: A decision framework for structuring browser agent harnesses across context storage, action execution, and auxiliary features.
- **Components**:
  - Context storage (screenshots, DOM, diffs, annotations)
  - Action execution (human-like, computer-like, coding agent, bash agent)
  - Harness features (subagents, compaction, memory)
- **When to use**: When designing and engineering web navigation agents.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Chat models failed to list Pokémon whose names ended in 'aw', but Claude Code wrote a python script to fetch all Pokémon and grep the result.
- **Illustrates**: Capability overhang and the power of giving models code execution arms.
- **Lesson**: Equipping models with execution tools bridges capability gaps.
### Transitioning from Opus 4 (calling AskUserQuestion with difficulty) to Opus 4.5 (interviewing users) to Opus 4.8 (building HTML reports and quizzes).
- **Illustrates**: The emergence of agentic properties and structured artifact generation.
- **Lesson**: Emergent tool use evolves rapidly across model generations.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Use blindspot pass prompts to help models uncover unknown unknowns in codebases.
  - Require agents to maintain implementation notes and log deviations.
  - Use HTML artifacts instead of raw markdown for complex multi-step agent plans.
- **Strategic**:
  - Treat LLM development more like biology than physics; rules are empirical and non-deterministic.
  - Reduce system prompt bloat as newer, smarter models are integrated.
  - Bridge the gap between the abstract map (prompt) and the actual territory (codebase/browser).
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - What is the optimal context storage strategy for browser agents?
  - How can compaction be automated without losing critical agent memory?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Models are grown, not designed. (conceptual)
- 80% of system prompts were removed from Claude Code while maintaining or improving performance. (anecdotal)
## Notable Quotes
> "Models are grown, not designed."
> "What contains them is us — the harness we put in, and the way we prompt them."
> "It's closer to a biology, than a physics."
## Compressed Summary
- AI models exhibit capability overhang where tools unlock dormant capabilities.
- System prompt design shifts from rigid constraints to model judgment as models improve.
- Managing unknown unknowns requires structured prompts like blindspot passes and implementation notes.
- Browser agent design requires careful architectural choices around context storage and action execution.
- **Keywords**: agents, prompting, harness, claude, browserbase
- **Core insight**: Building effective AI agents requires shifting from rigid rule-based constraints to empowering models with execution tools, smaller system prompts, and structured context management.
